title: Burst retry & backpressure sensitivity across cloud GPU lines
content:
Purpose
This is an exploratory working doc capturing experiments and early conclusions about how short, high-concurrency bursts (spikes of concurrent small requests) interact with driver and hardware characteristics across representative cloud GPU families (A100, H100, L40S) and common cloud SKUs. The goal: understand causes of observed retry/backpressure behavior, identify reproducible signals, and derive short-term mitigations we can ship in the serving runtime.

Summary (tl;dr)
- Short bursts (50–300 QPS with small payloads) produce disproportionate retry counts and higher p99 latency on some SKUs. The effect correlates with: (a) driver/CUDA version, (b) host->device submission path (PCIe vs NVLink), (c) scheduler preemption behavior when many small kernels are launched.
- H100 SKUs show higher resiliency to bursts in our tests (less retry amplification) when using newer drivers + CUDA 12.X, likely due to improved kernel dispatch batching in vendor stack.
- A100 SKUs with older drivers exhibit queue growth in the host-side submission path; retries are often due to runtime timeouts on our request queue rather than GPU OOM.
- L40S exhibits unusual behavior where high burst density causes interconnect transient slowdowns (host DMA backpressure) visible as correlated CPU-side stalls.

What we tested (experiment design)
- Workloads: small-token generation (prefill 16 tokens, decode 16 tokens) and short-chat-turn models (similar to 2–3k parameter baseline decoding patterns), chosen because they maximize kernel launch rate per second.
- Burst profiles: micro-burst (instantaneous concurrency ramp 0->200 in 500ms), sustained burst (200 QPS for 60s), and burst-with-noise (burst plus background 10 QPS steady traffic).
- Cloud SKUs: representative samples from primary clouds: A100 instance family (nv_***), H100 family (h***), L40S family (l***). We used the same model binary and quantization across runs to isolate hardware/driver effects.
- Driver/CUDA matrix: tested CUDA 11.8, 12.1, 12.2 and vendor driver variants (stock image vs. optimized driver).
- Instrumentation: eBPF on host to capture syscall/queue lengths, NVTX spans in runtime, per-kernel timestamps from cupti where available, host NIC and PCIe counters (through cloud SB counters), and application-level metrics (internal retry count, request latency buckets).

Key observations (detailed)
1) Host submission queue growth (A100, older drivers)
- On several A100 SKUs with driver X.Y (old), host-side submission queues (our runtime -> CUDA API calls) grew during micro-bursts. The GPU was not saturated; instead we saw 20–80ms stalls on cuLaunchKernel due to kernel-context switch amplification. Our request handler timed out waiting for in-flight slots and triggers a retry.
- eBPF traces show threads blocking on futexes inside the runtime queue consumer, correlated with a rapid spike in kernel launches.

2) Improved aggregation in newer stacks (H100, CUDA 12.x)
- On H100 with CUDA 12.2 and recent driver, observed fewer cuLaunchKernel stalls. Driver-level aggregation of small launches (and optimized kernel chaining) reduces syscall pressure and keeps p99 lower.
- Suggests vendor improvements are effective; we should track driver release notes and include recommended minimum driver/CUDA in our SKU support matrix.

3) Interconnect backpressure & DMA stalls (L40S)
- L40S runs showed spikes in host-side PCIe DMA latency when bursts overlapped with larger background transfers (e.g., checkpointing). This manifested as CPU-side stalls and occasional RPC timeouts.
- Correlation between NVME-backed KV spill activity and increased DMA latency suggests avoiding large host->device transfers concurrent with burst windows.

4) Retry root cause is often application-side timeouts
- Many retries come from our request-level timeout logic rather than fatal GPU errors. When kernel submission stalls, requests hit our retry threshold and are requeued, amplifying load and increasing queue pressure — a classic positive feedback loop.

Actionable mitigations (short term)
- Reduce aggressive request-level retry policy for small-prefill, bursty profiles; use jittered backoff and up to one retry instead of 3 within 1s. This reduces amplification.
- Introduce a burst admission controller in runtime: when submission queue depth > threshold, temporarily degrade new requests to best-effort (or route to fallback smaller model) rather than retry.
- Runtime: add micro-batching of kernel launches for small decode kernels where possible to reduce cuLaunch rate. Prototype exists (branch reference in linked artifacts).
- Ops: update recommended driver/CUDA minimums per SKU family in the console and onboarding docs (H100 + CUDA 12.2 recommended where available).

Longer-term experiments / engineering work
- Implement host-side async submission queue with backpressure signals that can be propagated back to API gateway to prevent retries.
- Test a hybrid submission that coalesces multiple small kernel launches into a single fused kernel where model architecture allows (requires ML model-level changes).
- Explore pinned-memory vs page-locked memory strategies for L40S to reduce DMA latency variance during heavy host traffic.

Open questions (to investigate next)
- Are there PCIe/NVLink firmware versions that correlate with observed DMA jitter on L40S? We need to expand vendor firmware matrix.
- Can we detect and classify "submission stall" vs "GPU saturation" in our tracing more reliably so the gateway can make smarter retry decisions? (Evan to prototype heuristics using eBPF + NVTX).
- For multi-tenant hosts, how much variance is due to noisy neighbors vs driver behavior? Need isolated single-tenant runs and controlled co-tenancy experiments.

Notes to self / experimental logs
- Attach raw traces to JIRA-RUN-7890 (linked_artifacts). Major trace file names: run-2025-11-18-a100-old-driver.tar.xz, run-2025-12-02-h100-cuda12.2.tar.xz, run-2026-02-14-l40s-dma-spike.tar.xz.
- Slack thread: #serving-runtime-bursts (see pinned message; Ben posted early pprof traces).

Immediate next steps (owners)
- Ben: prototype admission controller + backoff tuning (PR: linked_artifacts). Due: 2026-03-20.
- Marta: expanded driver/firmware sweep matrix for L40S (coordinate with cloud partners). Due: 2026-04-02.
- Evan: build heuristic to classify submission stalls vs GPU-saturation in our traces (use eBPF + cupti). Due: 2026-03-25.

Appendix (quick checklist for reruns)
- Ensure single-VM isolation for controlled runs.
- Run micro-burst profile with no background transfers, then with artificially injected host DMA.
- Collect eBPF, cupti, nvlink/pcie counters, and nginx/gRPC server metrics.
- Try both stock image driver and vendor-optimized driver images; record exact driver versions.

This doc is intentionally a working surface — expect fragmented notes, raw hypothesis checks, and TODOs. Feedback welcome; if you have a prioritized mitigation to try, add it to the action items and ping @Ben.
